story: A General Feedback Theory of Human Behavior (1960)
text: In psychology, this is called "Reinforcement"[1] and that goes back to Skinner (1938) and Thorndike (1911). In AI research its called "Reinforcement learning"[2]. One of the earliest papers relating reinforcement learning to AI was “Theory of Neural-Analog Reinforcement Systems”[3] by Minsky, 1954 A cool reinforcement learning demo is the DeepMind Atari video from last year[4] [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [LINK] [4] [VIDEO] (this is awesome)

story: Deep Learning – Review by LeCun, Bengio, and Hinton
text: I was also under the misapprehension that deep learning is just about classification, but that isn't true. Yes, reinforcement learning is the path to general intelligence, and the deep learning community is showing impressive progress on that front as well. The Deepmind demo [1] and the recent robotics work at Berkeley[2] are good examples. Thanks for the link to Stan Franklin's work. I'm glad to hear there is work to integrate the two approaches. story: Why 2015 Was a Breakthrough Year in Artificial Intelligence
text: AGI is the idea of creating general intelligence. Which almost certainly requires some reinforcement learning (the ways dogs and humans learn, by having a goal and an internal reward system). Deepmind's Atari player is based on deep reinforcement learning, where increasing the score represents a reward: [VIDEO] I used to believe the moving goalpost idea, that AI is anything that isn't yet possible. I now disagree. I saved myself a lot of energy by avoiding entirely the question "what counts as AI?" by switching to the question, "what counts as AGI?" which is a term with a clearer threshold: [LINK]
